principle: A persistent holographic person is not the same thing as a disposable holodeck character. Once person-level persistence is established, identity, memory, relationships and history remain attached to the same entity across activations and embodiments.
rules: Activation/deactivation does not create a new person each time.
Changing projection location or host system does not reroll identity.
A copied program is not automatically the same continuing person; continuity requires explicit copy/branch rules.
Memory persistence is authoritative state and cannot be assumed from a generic holographic template.
A disposable simulation character does not become a persistent person merely because AI generated dialogue for it.
Persistent holographic persons can accumulate relationships, knowledge, career and reputation when world/legal state permits.
Host-system access, permissions and mobility are operational constraints, not personality.
AI cannot promote a simulation character to persistent personhood, duplicate a person or restore a destroyed instance without authoritative events.
Visual projection remains linked to persistent identity unless the person intentionally changes avatar and that change is recorded.
unknown_policy: Specific EMH generations, mobile-emitter availability, legal personhood and copy/backup continuity require era/source-specific profiles.
ai_guardrails: Do not treat every hologram as a person.
Do not treat every persistent holographic person as an EMH.
Do not assume unlimited computer access or ship-wide omnipresence.
Do not duplicate one person by casually loading the same program twice without explicit branch/continuity rules.
academy_relevance: Teach only role-relevant computer, medical, legal or ethical constraints when a course requires them.
